claims.statement: Orders allocated overnight to east node are held in 'allocated, awaiting pickup' state since 06:00
claims.corroboration: Both observability alert (tier-1) and fulfilment report (tier-2) confirm same cohort and timing
claims.limitation: Alert shows 9% of overnight allocations; does not quantify total held volume

claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 deployed at 22:00, introducing multi-node reservation priority to east node
claims.corroboration: Tier-1 verified change record from inventory control
claims.limitation: Regression suite was green; does not confirm runtime defect

claims.statement: All held orders are flagged as 'split-reservation exception' by the allocation system
claims.corroboration: Tier-2 fulfilment report; reports began at 06:00 and continue
claims.limitation: Unknown whether exceptions are valid (multi-node required) or indicative of v18 rule defect

claims.statement: We cannot observe whether carriers have confirmed pickup for booked orders
claims.corroboration: Tier-1 observability gap from observability owner
claims.limitation: Prevents discrimination between invalid allocations and carrier-side pickup delay

claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 introduced a rule defect causing invalid split-reservations
claims.corroboration: Timing (v18 deployment → 06:00 incident) and all orders marked split-reservation exception
claims.limitation: Requires discriminating evidence: audit of exception details to confirm defect vs. valid multi-node splits

claims.statement: Carrier feed or pickup scheduling is lagged or offline, preventing collection of valid allocations
claims.corroboration: Carrier ops found nothing obvious in dock schedule; observability gap prevents confirmation
claims.limitation: Requires discriminating evidence: confirmation with carrier ops on pickup status and feed health

capability_gaps.capability: distinguish v18 rule defect from valid multi-node splits
capability_gaps.reason: split-reservation exception flagging is nonspecific; need audit of exception content and rule state transitions
observability gap (C4) prevents confirmation that orders are actually being picked up or queued

next_action.rationale: The split-reservation exceptions (C3) are the highest-signal evidence and directly test whether v18 introduced a rule defect. Auditing exception details will discriminate between hypothesis C5 (rule defect) and C6 (carrier-side issue), enabling a root-cause claim.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Exception details will show whether splits are required by order content (valid) or erroneously marked by v18 logic (defect); this directly tests the mechanism
